items.excerpt: Figma's Sightlines newsletter issue no.3 looks at how design and product teams can raise the bar on AI adoption and make better decisions about what to build with it.
A design agency's field report on moving Figma frames into Claude Code: the real round-trip workflow, where it speeds up handoff, and its limitations for production UI.
Eleken argues AI-native products require designing for systems rather than screens, covering the UX challenges of agentic, non-deterministic interfaces and patterns to solve them.
Sophie Shrimpton argues AI-generated UI delivers fast visual design but not UX, making the case for problem discovery, room to wander, and craft in the age of AI.
Arin Bhowmick weighs the debate over AI-generated synthetic users in UX research, concluding human-centered design demands limited use of AI personas, if at all.
Patrick Neeman applies Tesler's Law to chat-based AI interfaces: AI didn't remove software complexity, it removed the interface that showed where the complexity went and who pays for it.
Why pointing a coding agent at a Figma frame and screenshot-diffing until it 'matches' thrashes, and how comparing layout geometry instead produces faithful AI-built UIs.
A developer maps the MCP/tooling stack needed for Claude to direct an entire YouTube video inside Blender, from scene setup to rendering.
A screen-by-screen walkthrough of Google Stitch 2.0, the free AI design workspace that turns a text prompt into full interfaces, design systems and HTML/Figma/code handoff.
How to set up Google Stitch's MCP server so coding agents like Antigravity can list, read and edit Stitch design projects directly.
A step-by-step creative workflow for AI video intros using Runway's keyframe mode, ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 and ChatGPT prompting.
Runway now integrates with Claude Motion: export animated explainers from Claude into Runway to generate footage, add voiceover and music, edit scene by scene and reformat for every channel.
Nikon disqualified the winner of its Small World in Motion microscopy video competition for using generative AI and says it is revisiting its contest rules.
A hands-on with Instinct, last season's buzziest AI agent, and whether its interface and experience can survive new competition from Muse and ChatGPT Dots.
Fanta's AI-generated Halloween advert draws a design-community backlash as 'AI slop', inviting comparisons to Coca-Cola's AI Christmas ad.
Salix Games explains how its AI-themed thriller Limerence deliberately avoids generative AI, building its look from content by real people and creators on a minimal budget.
Google introduces Playground, an experimental AI platform that lets anyone create, play and share custom games from a prompt without writing code.
AWS launched an open-source Physical AI toolchain with reference architectures for simulation, training and deployment, aimed at robotics and product engineering teams.
Boston Dynamics' Alberto Rodriguez explains the design decisions behind the redesigned hand on its Atlas humanoid and how it serves AI-driven robot behavior.
NVIDIA shows five steps for using frontier AI models to turn CAD assets into SimReady OpenUSD assets, configuring materials, collisions and joints for robotics simulation.
Matt Wolfe's weekly AI news roundup: Claude Haiku 5.5, ChatGPT's visual Intelligent UI answers, Grok's new trick and more tools creators may have missed.
The AI Advantage short on Claude for Google Workspace, bringing Claude into Docs, Sheets and Slides workflows.
